question: Electromagnetic Induction was discovered by:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Faraday**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Michael Faraday discovered the principle of electromagnetic induction in 1831.
 
• Faraday’s law of electromagnetic induction states that an electromotive force is induced in a conductor when there is a change in the magnetic field around it.
 
• This discovery laid the foundation for the development of electric generators and transformers.
 
• Faraday's experiments demonstrated that a changing magnetic field could produce an electric current, which is the basic principle behind many types of electrical devices.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Electromagnetic Induction:**

 
 
• It is the production of voltage across a conductor situated in a changing magnetic field or a conductor moving through a stationary magnetic field.
 
• Faraday’s law mathematically describes how a time varying magnetic field creates an electric field.
 
• Electromagnetic induction is the working principle behind electrical components like inductors and transformers.
 
 
 
• **Lenz's Law:**
 
 
• Formulated by Heinrich Lenz in 1834, it states that the direction of the induced current will be such that it opposes the change in the magnetic field that produced it.
 
• Lenz's Law is a consequence of the law of conservation of energy.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Electromagnetic Induction:**
 
 
• Used in the generation of electric power in power plants.
 
• Essential in the functioning of transformers, which transfer electric energy between circuits.
 
• Induction motors utilize this principle to convert electrical energy into mechanical energy.
